name: number-input
purpose: Locale-aware numeric entry on a text input with the spinbutton role: parses and formats the locale's separators, digits, minus signs, and currency/percent/unit literals, steps with the keyboard and optional stepper buttons, and validates range and step with localized messages.
whenToUse: Quantities, amounts, prices, percentages, and measurements users type or adjust in small increments.
Numbers that must be entered and displayed in the user's locale (1.234,5 in German, Arabic-Indic digits in Arabic).
Values constrained by a minimum, maximum, or step.
whenNotToUse: Identifiers made of digits (card numbers, postal codes, phone numbers, one-time codes): use Text Input with inputMode 'numeric'.
Picking a value on a continuous range where precision does not matter: use Slider.
Dates and times: use Date Input or Date Picker.
responsive: Full width of its container; the stepper buttons keep their size and the input shrinks (min-inline-size 0). Density tokens adjust the control height and button size.
rtl: Logical properties: the stepper buttons sit at the inline end in both directions. Bidi control marks Intl inserts in RTL locales are ignored when parsing.
theme: Control surface, border, focus, error, hover, disabled, and sunken-surface role tokens. Focus is shown on the control boundary with a 1px ring plus border color. Forced-colors mode draws a Highlight outline on focus and GrayText for disabled steppers.
security: Label, help text, formatted values, and messages are rendered with textContent or attributes. Validation messages never include the entered text; only constraint parameters. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. A hidden input named `name` carries the canonical value (for example 1234.5) for native form submission; the visible input is not named.

performance.testedScale: Target: 1,000 inputs on one page (performance test pending the e2e harness entry).

limitations: Values are JavaScript numbers (IEEE 754 doubles): integers beyond 2^53 and more than about 15 significant digits are not exact. Use Text Input for arbitrary-precision decimals.
Parsing follows the locale strictly: in de-DE a typed '.' is a group separator, so '1.5' is 15.
Group separators are accepted anywhere in the integer part; their positions are not validated.
Accounting formats (parentheses for negatives), scientific, engineering, and compact notation are not parsed.
The canonical value in the hidden input uses JavaScript number serialization, which is exponent notation below 1e-6 and from 1e21.
With inputMode 'numeric' (maximumFractionDigits 0) some mobile keyboards have no minus key; set min >= 0 or use the default decimal format for signed integers.
Stepper buttons do not repeat on press-and-hold.
unsupported: Native type=number behavior (wheel stepping, browser-specific spin buttons).
Rendering HTML in the label, help text, or messages.
antiPatterns: Using Number Input for codes and identifiers that are not quantities.
Setting a step larger than the range between min and max.
Using percent style with step 1 (that is 100 percentage points); the percent default is 0.01.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/number-input: AuiNumberInput directive ([auiNumberInput]) with ControlValueAccessor and Validator.
adapters.react: @absoluteui/react/number-input: AuiNumberInput component; controlled (value/defaultValue + onValueChange) or uncontrolled.
